newsitem.title: FRANCE: Portugal expects $6 bln from privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Portugal expects $6 bln from privatisation.

text.p: Portuguese Economy Minister Augusto Mateus, heading a team of economic experts, told Algerian officials on Sunday his country expected privatisation to bring in $6 billion in 1996 and 1997.
The official Algerian news agency APS said Mateus gave the figure to a seminar in Algiers during a two-day visit that included briefing Algerians on Portugal's privatisation.
It said the minister told the group that Portugal had started with "viable sectors which were operating well", such as banks and insurance companies.
Privatisation was advancing at a "progressive and encouraging rhythm" with the main aim of creating managerial capacity and opening up competitiveness among companies.

The head of the Arab-Portuguese Chamber, Angelo Correa, told the seminar that privatisation had been chosen as the best way of reducing treasury indebtedness, diversifying capital and assuring the competitiveness of public companies.
But he said that for it to succeed unions must be involved, APS quoted him as saying.

The agency said later that Mateus held talks with Algerian Energy Minister Amar Makhloufi who discussed with the visiting minister possible cooperation in processing materials such as phosphates and Algerian involvement in distributing energy products in Portugal.
Mateus was welcomed at the airport late on Saturday by Algerian State Secretary for Cooperation and Maghreb Arab Affairs, Lahcene Moussaoui, with whom he is to have detailed talks.
In November, Algerian, Moroccan, Spanish and Portuguese energy ministers officially opened the natural gas pipeline running from Algeria to Spain and linking up with Portugal.
APS said that Sonatrach had also concluded a deal with the Portuguese firm NAIGAS to deliver 2.1 billion cubic metres of natural liquefied gas. It gave no further details.
